result.text:
Done. All 56 tests pass (the 16 original ones unchanged).

## What I built

**Ground types + sonar** (`ground.py`, `firm_sand.py`, `silt.py`, `boulder.py`, `sonar.py`)
`Ground` answers two messages — `move_crawler_towards(a_crawler, a_direction)` and `assert_crawler_can_turn(a_crawler)` — so boulder/silt/sand behaviour is polymorphic, with no conditionals added to the movement code. The crawler asks the sonar for the ground of the **destination** when moving, and of its **current position** when turning. `Sonar.with_grounds({...})` answers `FirmSand()` for unknown positions, so `at_facing` still works (it uses `Sonar.all_firm_sand()`); `at_facing_sonar` is the new constructor. `Silt` owns the sliding rule (`randrange(10) + 1`, i.e. 1..10 cells) and takes its random injected, so the tests are deterministic via a `FixedRandom` double.

**Guarded runs** (`crawler_run.py`, `normal_run.py`, `guarded_run.py`, `crawler_movement.py` + 3 subclasses)
The crawler's current run is a state object handling `(` / `)` and the three things that differ between runs: starting/finishing, moving onto silt (normal slides, guarded signals), and registering movements to undo. `GuardedRun` keeps a stack of `CrawlerDisplacement` / `CrawlerClockwiseTurn` / `CrawlerCounterClockwiseTurn`, each of which knows its opposite movement; on any error `process` pops the stack and re-raises with a bare `raise`. In a `NormalRun` all of that is a no-op, so behaviour outside parentheses is exactly the first version's.

**Repeated commands**
A digit repeats the last command `digit + 2` more times; any non-repeatable command (invalid one, digit, parenthesis) forgets it, so `"0"`, `"a00"`, `"(0)"` and `"(a)0"` are all invalid commands.

## Tests added (37 new)

Repetition (including each command, the digit boundaries, and the three ways a digit is invalid), boulders (advance, retreat, both turns, and a boulder interrupting a repetition), silt (slide 1 and 10 cells, retreating, turning unaffected, ground under the crawler irrelevant when moving, plus a 100-run bounds check with the real random), and guarded runs (commit on success, undo of moves/turns/repetitions, silt and invalid commands inside, nesting, unfinished, `)` without `(`, several runs in one sequence, and that a finished run is not undone by a later error).

Two cases worth flagging, since the statement doesn't decide them: a digit after `(` or `)` is an invalid command (a parenthesis is not repeatable), and `")"` without an open parenthesis gets its own error rather than being silently ignored. The README has a new "Second version" section documenting the design.
